extracted.intended_audience: Recipients of NEH Public Scholar Program awards (awardees and their institutional administrators)
extracted.subtask_description: Terms and conditions that NEH Public Scholar award recipients must follow while administering and completing their award, including administrative, financial, programmatic, and legal requirements. Covers eligibility constraints, reporting, travel, payments, recordkeeping, and prohibitions on uses of funds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification of institutional affiliation
rubrics_metrics.description: If you have an academic institutional affiliation, NEH requires you to notify your department chair, chief academic officer, and director of sponsored research that NEH has offered you an award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This notification is required upon award offer; no further procedural detail except to contact Public Scholar Program with questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance via eGMS Reach Individual Program Acceptance Form
rubrics_metrics.description: To accept the award, you must complete and submit the NEH Individual Program Acceptance Form through eGMS Reach by the deadline indicated in your offer letter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The form is located in the Forms & Reports tab of your offer in eGMS Reach. Learn how to access eGMS Reach or contact the Public Scholar Program for help.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipient legal, financial, administrative, and programmatic responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients assume legal, financial, administrative, and programmatic responsibility for administering their award in accordance with this document and the award documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to comply may result in suspension or termination and NEH recovery of funds. Recipients must inform NEH of significant issues during the award period.

rubrics_metrics.name: NEH Office roles and award authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Only the NEH Office of Grant Management is authorized to issue the notice of award that obligates NEH funds or to change funding, duration, or other terms of an award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NEH program officers handle programmatic aspects; Office of Accounting manages ACH/payment processing; Office of Inspector General handles audits and investigations. Applicants/recipients should rely on the Office of Grant Management for official award actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time commitment and period of performance limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Project periods may range between a minimum of six months and a maximum of twelve months; the period must be continuous. Recipients must work at least half-time on their projects for the entire period and must work a minimum of six full-time months or the equivalent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part-time is defined as between half-time and full-time. Recipients who teach while working part-time must reduce teaching load proportionately. Full-time awardees must forgo other major activities, including teaching. The period of performance may not be less than six months or exceed twelve months and you must complete your project work plan within twelve months of your chosen start date. The time period and commitment indicated on the acceptance form are subject to NEH approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concurrent funding restrictions (NEH specific)
rubrics_metrics.description: You may concurrently hold non-NEH funding for the same project, but you may not accept or hold more than one NEH individual award in a given federal fiscal year and you may not hold a Public Scholar award for work on a project previously supported by an NEH Fellowship or an Award for Faculty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may not work on a project supported by an NEH institutional award while holding an NEH individual award on a full-time basis. Contact NEH staff before accepting if you have questions about multiple NEH awards or publisher advances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on work leading toward degrees
rubrics_metrics.description: You may audit courses and seminars pertinent to your project, but you may not enroll in a degree program or engage in work you intend to apply toward a degree either now or later.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Auditing relevant courses is allowed; any activity intended to count toward a degree is prohibited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledgment and required disclaimer
rubrics_metrics.description: All materials resulting from activities under an award must contain an acknowledgment of NEH support and include the statement: 'Any views, findings, conclusions, or recommendations expressed in the (publication) (program) (website) do not necessarily reflect those of the National Endowment for the Humanities.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NEH provides additional information, media tips, and suggestions at NEH's publicizing-your-project resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment procedures and ACH form submission
rubrics_metrics.description: NEH will send a Notice of Action containing payment schedule and instructions to submit banking information via the ACH Vendor/Miscellaneous Payment Enrollment Form SF-3881; NEH cannot pay you until you submit this form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For awards issued August 12, 2024 or later, NEH no longer requires a signature on the ACH form. Do not attach payment requests to eGMS Reach messages or emails. The ACH form is in Forms & Reports in eGMS Reach.

rubrics_metrics.name: ACH/bank account requirements and tips
rubrics_metrics.description: Funds must be transferred directly to a checking or savings account (not a trust). Routing and account numbers must be accurate (routing number is 9 digits); include hyphens in account number but omit spaces and special symbols.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use deposit slips. If the first two digits of the routing number are not in specified ranges (01-12, 21-32, 61-72), direct deposit may be rejected. If check indicates payable through another bank, contact your financial institution for correct routing number. Checking account number can be up to 17 digits; do not include the check number.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal debt delinquency restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients may not be delinquent in the repayment of any federal debt. If you become delinquent during performance, you must notify NEH immediately and provide evidence of an IRS repayment agreement and current payments before NEH will release funds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include student loans, delinquent federal taxes, delinquent child support, and delinquent payroll taxes. See OMB Circular A-129 for further guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equipment definition and Buy American encouragement
rubrics_metrics.description: Equipment is tangible, nonexpendable personal property with useful life >1 year and acquisition cost ≥ $5,000 per unit. If you purchase equipment/products ≥ $10,000 per unit with NEH funds, you should purchase American-made equipment/products consistent with Executive Order 13788.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an encouragement (not an absolute prohibition) and does not apply to commercial information technology.

rubrics_metrics.name: No medical insurance or fringe benefits provided
rubrics_metrics.description: NEH provides neither medical insurance nor any other fringe benefits for awardees; NEH awards to individuals do not cover unemployment compensation or Social Security insurance because recipients are not U.S. government employees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NEH recommends considering continuation of any benefit programs in which you participate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tax treatment — NEH does not withhold taxes or provide tax advice
rubrics_metrics.description: NEH does not withhold Social Security, state, or federal income taxes from your award and does not send 1099s or other tax forms. NEH cannot provide tax advice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Direct specific tax questions to the IRS, state/local officials, or your tax advisor. See IRS interactive tax assistant for guidance on scholarship/fellowship income.

rubrics_metrics.name: Domestic airfare and travel cost limit
rubrics_metrics.description: Airfare for domestic travel charged to the award may not exceed the value of the basic least expensive unrestricted accommodations class offered by commercial airlines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Charge the basic least expensive unrestricted accommodations class; NEH expects compliance with federal travel cost principles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign travel airfare limits and Fly America Act compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Airfare for foreign travel paid with NEH funds may not exceed the basic least expensive unrestricted accommodations class. All air transportation paid in whole or part with NEH funds must be performed on a U.S. flag air carrier in accordance with the Fly America Act (49 U.S.C. 40118), except in permitted circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permissible exceptions include: transportation under an 'Open Skies' agreement where allowed, involuntary rerouting (U.S. carrier involuntarily reroutes via foreign carrier), specific open-skies/route exceptions, short-distance travel, and other regulatory exceptions described in 41 CFR 301-10.131-143 and GSA guidance. Lower cost, convenience, or traveler preference are NOT acceptable reasons to use a foreign carrier. See page for detailed exception conditions (e.g., timing thresholds, number of aircraft changes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of foreign-flag carriers: detailed exception conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific conditions allow foreign-flag air carriers: Open Skies agreements (e.g., U.S./EU rules), involuntary rerouting, travel where U.S.-flag service would extend time by set thresholds, short-distance travel (elapsed flight time ≤ 3 hours), or when use eliminates multiple aircraft changes or long connections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed numeric thresholds and conditions are provided (e.g., 24-hour/6-hour/4-hour/three-hour rules). Consult cited regulations and GSA/Open Skies guidance for route-specific applicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on political, religious, or ideological advocacy
rubrics_metrics.description: NEH funds may not be used for promotion of a particular political, religious, or ideological point of view; advocacy for a particular program of social or political action; or support of specific public policies or legislation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See also the separate prohibition on use of funds for lobbying activities (Byrd Anti-Lobbying Amendment and 18 U.S.C. 1913) which lists unallowable charges such as electioneering activities, financial support for political parties, and attempts to influence legislation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Change requests for project scope or work plan require prior NEH approval
rubrics_metrics.description: You may not change project scope, work plan, period of performance, or reporting due dates without prior NEH approval. All requests must be submitted through eGMS Reach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To request a scope/work plan change, use the Changes Requests tab → 'Scope and/or Work Plan Amendment Request', describe and justify changes in writing, and submit as soon as possible but no later than 30 days prior to the end of period of performance. NEH will determine whether changes fall within the intent of the award; approval is not guaranteed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Change requests for period of performance or report due dates and timelines
rubrics_metrics.description: To request a change in the period of performance, submit an 'Extension Request' via eGMS Reach at least 30 days before the end date; to request a report due date extension select that option and submit at least 30 days before the report is due.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approval of extensions may impact payment schedules. Amendments are considered case-by-case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final performance report submission and deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: You must submit a final performance report on activities accomplished with your NEH award electronically via eGMS Reach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you received your award on or after November 12, 2020, the final report is due within 120 days of the end of performance; if before that date, within 90 days. No final financial report is required. Submit via Reports tab in eGMS Reach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission of award products to NEH
rubrics_metrics.description: One copy of all award products should be forwarded to NEH as soon as they are available, regardless of how long after grant completion the publication may appear.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This applies to publications or other products resulting from award-supported activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record retention requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: You are required to maintain a record of all documents pertinent to your award for a period of three years from the date you submit your Final Performance Report to the NEH.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep all documentation that supports use of funds, performance, and compliance for this retention period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyright and NEH royalty-free rights
rubrics_metrics.description: You may copyright works developed under your NEH award. NEH reserves a royalty-free, non-exclusive, and irrevocable right to reproduce, publish, or otherwise use NEH-supported work for federal purposes and to authorize others to do so.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NEH may request excerpts for publication and may ask recipients to participate in NEH-sponsored public events; recipients agree, on mutually acceptable terms, to participate if requested and to provide advance notice of public appearances to facilitate NEH publicity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure/publication of application narrative and bibliography (FOIA/sample apps)
rubrics_metrics.description: In accordance with the Freedom of Information Act, NEH may make available to the public the narrative and bibliography you submitted, for example as samples of successful applications on NEH's website or at applicant workshops.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware that application materials may be published by NEH for training or outreach purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Library of Congress Cataloging in Publication (CIP) recommendation
rubrics_metrics.description: NEH strongly recommends cataloging any publication resulting from the award under the Library of Congress CIP Program before final printing to facilitate library acquisition and dissemination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publishers ineligible for CIP may be eligible for Preassigned Card Number Program; entering titles in a national bibliographic database increases dissemination.

rubrics_metrics.name: State humanities council notification
rubrics_metrics.description: You must notify your state humanities council of your award and, wherever possible, give advance notice of any related public events occurring in the state.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A list of state humanities councils is available on NEH's website.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research misconduct policy and consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: NEH will take appropriate action against individuals/organizations upon determination that misconduct occurred in proposing, performing, reviewing, or reporting research funded by NEH, in accordance with the NEH Research Misconduct Policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research misconduct includes fabrication, falsification, plagiarism, and other specified behaviors; consult NEH Research Misconduct Policy for procedures and sanctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on use of funds for lobbying (Byrd Anti-Lobbying Amendment and 18 U.S.C. 1913)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients may not use appropriated funds to influence the Executive or Legislative Branches in connection with a covered award (31 U.S.C. 1352). 18 U.S.C. 1913 makes it a crime to use appropriated funds to influence members of Congress regarding legislation or appropriations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unallowable charges include certain electioneering activities, financial support for political parties, attempts to influence federal/state legislation, and certain legislative liaison activities. The full text of 18 U.S.C. 1913 is included in award documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with the Drug-Free Workplace Act reporting requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must comply with the Drug-Free Workplace Act of 1988 (2 CFR part 3373) and may not engage in unlawful manufacture, distribution, possession, or use of controlled substances in conducting grant activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If convicted of a criminal drug offense resulting from conduct during grant activity, report the conviction in writing to the Office of Grants Management within ten calendar days, including the federal award identification number of each affected award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with federal labor standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must comply with labor standards set out in Labor Standards on Projects or Productions Assisted by Grants from the NEA and NEH (see 29 CFR part 505).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comply with the cited CFR part for employment/labor-related requirements when applicable to projects or productions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Termination and repayment obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: NEH may terminate your award if you discontinue the proposed program before the end of performance or fail to observe the award’s terms and conditions. If you discontinue early you must return any funds received over those to which you are entitled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If unable to meet terms during performance, inform NEH immediately. Because stipends are paid in advance, you may be required to return a portion of the stipend; NEH will inform you of amount, basis for calculation, and repayment date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Debarment and eligibility restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients may not be debarred, suspended, proposed for debarment, declared ineligible, or voluntarily excluded from covered transactions; within the three years preceding application they may not have been convicted of or had a civil judgment for listed offenses in connection with public transactions. Debarment will result in immediate termination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed offenses include fraud, antitrust violations, embezzlement, theft, forgery, bribery, falsification/destruction of records, making false statements, receiving stolen property, termination for cause/default, or being presently indicted or charged. See 2 CFR Parts 180 and 3369 for details.
